claim.anchor: Bisbee, Arizona — Warren Mining District, Cochise County. Laramide quartz-monzonite porphyry intruding Paleozoic Escabrosa Limestone + Abrigo Formation. Major Cu-Ag-Au district (~8 Mt Cu, ~25 Moz Ag, ~3 Moz Au historically).

aspirational.reason: Siderite is documented district-wide and as a Bisbee post-mining product, but the corrected mass-balanced cavity path does not deliver it in the three-seed panel; it remains a documented possibility, not a deterministic promise.

Galena is documented in the Warren District, but the former late PbS occurrence depended on oxic sulfate being treated as sulfide. The valence-correct trajectory supplies no reproducible Pb-sulfide window, so it is a documented possibility rather than a deterministic product.

excluded_species.amosite: The current district-wide 300+ species inventory does not document amosite, and the Fe-Mg amphibole asbestos belongs to metamorphosed iron formations rather than this porphyry-carbonate-replacement system.
excluded_species.arsenopyrite: The current district-wide Bisbee species inventory does not document arsenopyrite; arsenic is instead carried by documented tennantite-group and oxidized arsenate phases.
excluded_species.millerite: The current district-wide Bisbee species inventory does not document millerite, so Ni must not precipitate as a discrete NiS phase here.
excluded_species.realgar: The current district-wide Bisbee species inventory does not document realgar; the scenario's arsenic belongs to Cu sulfosalts and late arsenates.
excluded_species.pararealgar: The district record does not support a realgar parent, so its light-induced pararealgar product is also excluded.
excluded_species.erythrite: The current district-wide Bisbee species inventory does not document erythrite; the earlier large Co loading was based on an unsupported locality inference.
excluded_species.annabergite: The current district-wide Bisbee species inventory does not document annabergite; the earlier large Ni loading was based on an unsupported locality inference.
excluded_species.halite: The current district-wide Bisbee and post-mining species inventories do not document halite; soluble sulfate crusts are documented, but the simulator must not force NaCl with an artificial salinity jump.

notes: Anchor: Bisbee, Arizona — Warren Mining District, Cochise County. Host: combo Laramide quartz-monzonite porphyry intruded into Paleozoic Escabrosa Limestone + Abrigo Formation. In the sim this is represented as a limestone wall (the pH buffer, the CO3 source for azurite) with scenario events that inject dissolved SiO2 from the surrounding silicate matrix weathering — the supply path for late chrysocolla.

Centerpiece mechanic: the azurite → malachite → chrysocolla cascade. Azurite dominates at high pCO2 (event 6, CO3 >= 120 ppm). A pCO2-drop event (event 7) dissolves azurite and fires malachite. A silica-seep event (event 8) dissolves malachite-without-silica and fires chrysocolla pseudomorphs on the remaining azurite crystals. Three carbonate/silicate phases recording three different groundwater chemistries, each one freezing a different step of the Cochise County monsoon.

Chemistry-audit gap-fill pass (Apr 2026): Ag=40 (Bisbee was a major Ag producer ~25 Moz; argentiferous galena + tetrahedrite + argentite + minor native Ag per Graeme et al. 2019). Mg=50 (Escabrosa Limestone host dolomitic in places; brief-required non-zero baseline). P=5 (enables pyromorphite given Pb+Cl already populated). Sb=5 (tetrahedrite trace; completes the Sb-As-Bi greisen triplet). Au=3 (Bisbee ~3 Moz historically — Cu-Au porphyry; native gold + auriferous chalcocite per Graeme 2019).

SIM 261 source reconciliation: the current district-wide 300+ species list does not contain cobaltite, nickeline, safflorite, erythrite, annabergite, millerite, amosite, arsenopyrite, realgar/pararealgar, or halite. The unsupported Co=80/Ni=70 loading was removed, and explicit locality exclusions now prevent chemically permissive global engines from inventing those phases here.
